accolade: Colle = neck: a hug or a tap on the shoulder from the king. Now: a prize, high praise.
Accolade: the award speech where the whole room applauds you.
admonish: Ad + monere: like a hall monitor who warns you. “Don’t run!”
Admonish gently: a firm but friendly reprimand.
antithetical: Anti + thesis: the exact opposite of what you said. Fire is antithetical to ice.
Antithetical views: two debaters on opposite sides of the stage.
arbitrary: Arbiter: a judge who picks on a whim. An arbitrary rule has no logic.
Arbitrary = picked by dice. “Why 3 pm? No reason.”
arcane: Arca = chest: the secrets locked away. Arcane rituals only the initiated know.
Arcane knowledge: dusty manuscripts and spells.
audacity: Audere: dare. Audacity can be brave or cheeky: “the audacity!”
Audacity: asking the CEO for a pay rise on day one.
austere: Austère: bare walls, no decoration. An austere monk’s cell.
Austere = strict and plain: a Calvinist church.
brazen: Brass face: you can’t blush through it. A brazen thief who steals in daylight.
Brazen = shameless: lying right to your face.
circumscribe: Circum + scribere: draw a circle around. The law circumscribes your powers.
Circumscribe: set limits, like a chalk circle around a child.
constituent: Constitute: a part that makes up the whole. An ingredient; a voter in your district.
Constituent = the person who constitutes your electorate.
dilettante: Diletto (Italian): delight. A dabbler who dips into painting, then pottery.
Dilettante: has fifteen hobbies and mastered none.
foment: Fomentare (to warm): keep a rebellion warm until it hatches. Foment unrest.
A hot-water compress: foment = apply heat; now to stir up trouble.
garrulous: Garrulus: a chattering jay. A garrulous neighbour at the bus stop.
Garrulous = gargling words: talking too much about nothing.
gauche: Gauche: left-handed, so clumsy. A gauche remark at dinner.
Gauche = awkward in company: you step on the host’s toes.
haphazard: Hap = chance, hazard: whatever happens. A haphazard pile of papers.
hegemony: Hegemon: leader. The hegemony of Rome over the Mediterranean.
Hegemony: one big power dominating the rest, like a school’s top clique.
inimical: In-amicus: not a friend. Inimical to peace: acts as its enemy.
Inimical = enemy-like: a climate inimical to crops.
inscrutable: In + scrutari (search): can’t be searched out. The Sphinx’s face.
An inscrutable smile: you stare and learn nothing.
insolent: In + solere (be accustomed): not behaving as is customary. A cheeky pupil.
Insolent: talks back to the teacher.
intrepid: In + trepidus (alarmed): no fear. An intrepid explorer.
Intrepid: wades into the jungle without a tremble.
inveterate: Vetus = old: old habit. An inveterate liar has lied for years.
Inveterate = a veteran of the habit: the chain smoker since age 14.
irrevocable: Ir + revocare: can’t call back. An irrevocable decision, no return.
Irrevocable: the arrow has left the bow.
lionize: Treat someone like a lion: make a celebrity. The town lionized the hero.
Lionize: crowds mobbing the author at a book signing.
munificent: Munus = gift: a munificent donor gives lavishly.
Munificent: opens his wallet like a fountain.
myriad: Myrias: 10,000. A myriad stars in the desert sky.
obsequious: Ob + sequi (follow): follows you around nodding. An obsequious waiter bowing repeatedly.
Obsequious: sucking up. The intern laughing at all the boss’s jokes.
ostracize: Ostrakon: a pot-shard used to vote someone out of Athens. To shun.
Ostracize = send to Coventry: nobody talks to the outcast.
pedestrian: Pedes = foot: walks instead of flies. A pedestrian speech: plodding, dull.
Pedestrian prose: a flat road with no view.
pernicious: Per + nex (death): deadly in the long run. A pernicious lie spreading in a community.
poignant: Pungere (prick): a pang in the heart. A poignant farewell.
Poignant: an old couple holding hands at the grave.
precipitous: Precipice: a sheer cliff. A precipitous decline.
Precipitous slope: hold on or fall.
prodigious: Prodigy: amazing. A prodigious appetite or talent.
prolific: Proles = offspring: lots of children, or lots of books. A prolific author.
Prolific: a rabbit’s family or a novelist’s output.
propitious: Propitius: kind, favourable. A propitious moment to ask for a raise.
ravenous: Ravine/rapere: seize. Eat like a wolf: ravenous.
Ravenous after a ten-mile hike: you could eat anything.
repudiate: Repudium: Roman divorce. Repudiate = cast off a claim or a spouse.
Repudiate: publicly reject what was said in your name.
rescind: Re + scindere (cut): cut away the decision. The company rescinded the job offer.
Rescind = undo an order, as a law is repealed.
resurgent: Re + surgere: rise again. A resurgent economy after the crash.
reverent: Revere: deep respect. Reverent silence in a cathedral.
Reverent: taking off your hat as the flag passes.
sanction: A contranym: to approve or to punish. Check the context: “sanctioned the plan” vs “sanctions on Russia”.
Sanction = “sanctify”: a stamp of authority. The council sanctioned the merger.
scrupulous: Scrupulus: a tiny sharp stone. A scrupulous person feels the stone and corrects it.
sporadic: Sporas = scattered (spores). Sporadic rain: a few drops here and there.
Sporadic gunfire: now and then, no pattern.
subversive: Sub + vertere: turn from below. A subversive pamphlet.
Subversive art: smuggling rebellion under the censor’s nose.
sycophant: Sykophantes: “fig-shower”. Today the yes-man who flatters the king.
Sycophant: the aide who laughs at the boss’s weakest jokes.
taciturn: Tacere: be silent. A taciturn farmer: “Yup.”
tempered: Tempered steel: heated and cooled to the right hardness; tempered opinions: softened.
Tempered = adjusted, moderated, like a chocolate.
tractable: Tractor-able: you can pull it along. A tractable horse.
Tractable: a student who does what he’s told.
trite: Tritus: worn out by rubbing. “All’s well that ends well”: trite.
Trite = over-polished: a cliché rubbed smooth.
vacillate: Vacillare: to sway. Candle flame back and forth; torn between two options.
Vacillate: can’t decide between pizza or pasta, for an hour.
winsome: Win + some: you win people over. A winsome smile.
